question.question:
For a 12-month year, a company has net income 2300000 USD, preferred dividends 60000 USD and 1000000 ordinary shares outstanding on day one, and issues 180000 shares at the start of month 10, weighted by whole months from month 10 through 12 over 12. Basic EPS is net income less preferred dividends over weighted shares. Potential shares: (1) 100000 shares issuable for no consideration if year-end revenue is at least 5000000 USD; actual revenue is 5750000 USD. If met, they are unissued, excluded from basic EPS and included in diluted EPS all year with no earnings adjustment; otherwise excluded. (2) 200000 options, exercise price 20 USD, average market price 19 USD; treasury stock method applies only if market price exceeds exercise price, else no incremental shares. (3) Convertible bonds outstanding all year, face 2000000 USD, coupon 11 percent, convertible into 50000 shares with full-year conversion; tax rate 25 percent. Sequential test: include the zero-incremental instruments (contingent shares and options) first, then the bonds only if their after-tax interest add-back per conversion share is strictly below diluted EPS computed with all prior inclusions. Compute diluted EPS; do not round intermediates.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Exact weighted average ordinary shares for basic EPS.
Exact basic EPS after preferred dividends.
Exact incremental shares from options under the treasury stock method.
Exact after-tax interest add-back per bond conversion share.
